p.x:
I want to reiterate that this bill is a nightmarish piece of nonsense that is **against** AI safety. I don't understand how even Stop/Pause/MIRI people could support this unless they actually want to bring about the forever war apocalypse.

This bill defines superintelligence as an AI system that can "undermine the US government". This definition means that any AI system, even something as simple as a facial recognition suite with a transformer attached that is designed to reduce bias and false positives on matches could be defined as "ASI" if it fails to function in accordance with the desires of a mass surveillance regime.

As it is written, this is a tool for the US government to nationalize anything and anyone engaged with transformers, RNNs, CNNs, even n-grams lol, under the threat of up to 20 years in prison. This bill could even define Pangram as ASI if it was used to point out that government issued statements or executive orders contained AI writing.

This is one of the most ill-informed and dystopian pieces of proposed legislation I have seen in my life, on par with things like the patriot act and the recent authorizations that allow the executive branch to declare any area in the country a "National Security Area" and deploy military forces to arrest people in it.

We are sliding into authoritarianism and x-risk discourse is getting absorbed into that push while naively thinking their concerns are being taken seriously instead of being used and manipulated to feed the existing totalitarian trend.

p.x:
Elon Musk proposes a massive idea to solve AI's compute problem for inferencing. 🤯

He says idling Tesla cars could create massive 100million-vehicle strong computer for AI - generating 100 Gigawatts of distributed compute power.

And these cars already have power and cooling built-in.

The back-of-the-envelope math assumes roughly 1 kW of usable inference per car, and multiplying that by 100M cars yields 100 GW, which is data-center scale but distributed across streets and garages.

This is similar in spirit to old volunteer grids like SETI@home, but here the nodes are mobile, intermittently connected, and thermally limited, which makes scheduling, reliability, and heat management a first-class problem.

Real workloads would need to be tolerant to variable latency and churn, for example batched media transcodes, large language model inference that is not real-time, or offline embedding generation.

Networking still will be the choke point because home Wi-Fi and cellular uplinks cap how fast model weights, prompts, and results can move, so caching and small model variants would be required.

Also, if it happens, energy and cost flow need a clean deal for owners, covering electricity, hardware wear, and bandwidth, likely with opt-in controls and clear limits to avoid battery drain and excess heat.

Further issue will be around Security and privacy. Inferencing compute must isolate tenant code from the car’s driving stack, with strong sandboxing, attestation, and remote kill-switches.

On vehicles, Musk said the AI5 computer targets up to 40x the AI4/HW4 performance, aiming to unlock autonomy improvements he frames as roughly 10x safer than human driving.

---

p.x:
Elon Musk on Creating Grokipedia: Rethinking the Future of Online Information

Elon Musk shared his vision behind Grokipe­dia describing it as a superior alternative to Wikipedia more neutral, accurate, and comprehensive. 

According to Musk Grokipedia was built using the latest version of Grok, a truth-seeking AI model trained to break down arguments into fundamental axioms that are likely true and non-contradictory. 

By doing so Grok ensures that conclusions follow logically from sound premises, leading to higher-quality reasoning and analysis. Musk explained that his team trained Grok extensively in critical thinking.

They used it to review, correct, and enhance over a million of Wikipedia’s most popular articles researching the broader internet to fix factual errors, eliminate bias, and add deeper context.

We didn’t just copy Wikipedia, Musk emphasized. We improved it.

He believes Grokipedia’s viral growth will be self-reinforcing. As users cite it on websites, share it on social media, and click on Grokipedia results in search engines, its credibility and ranking will naturally rise. 

Musk expects that readers familiar with a topic will quickly recognize its superiority: “When people read about a subject they know well and see how much more comprehensive and accurate it is, they’ll realize this is the better source.”

Looking ahead, Musk revealed plans to integrate Grok Imagine to generate explanatory videos directly from Grokipedia articles. 

This feature will transform static text into dynamic visual explanations whether for chemical reactions, medical concepts, or any other topic. 

If you’re trying to learn something he said, you’ll be able to highlight any part of the text and have Grok explain it right there.

Musk expressed full confidence in Grokipedia’s success, calling Wikipedia a not-very-good product often wrong, out of date, with few images and no real interactivity.

In contrast Grokipedia aims to be accurate, rich in multimedia, and deeply engaging. It’s not going to be a little bit better than Wikipedia, Musk declared. It’s going to be a hundred times better.

He also reflected on the broader challenge of human belief systems and confirmation bias: It’s remarkable how much people believe simply because it’s the view of their in-group. 

Some will cling to their ideological or tribal beliefs no matter what. Even if the evidence is staring them in the face, they’ll refuse to see it.

You can’t convince a flat-earther the world is round because to them, every piece of evidence is just part of the lie.

p.x: I can't stop thinking about the neurofeedback experiments I ran in my undergrad lab's tiny and underfunded building. Though my approach was rudimentary at the time, the signs are all around us that neurotech is beginning to feel the impact of intelligence acceleration - and not a moment too late. When I first dropped out of college to come ride the Great Wave with the rest of you in San Francisco, I had finished all the Cognitive Science courses I would need for my degree - "French 101" was all that kept me from graduating. I have no regrets, though, since I am well-positioned to do what I came here to do, and my time spent in school is proving more useful than I thought now that I'm refocusing my efforts around pointing AGI at human exocortical enhancement (alongside my day-job of... helping solve alignment). The future must have a place for us, and advancing neurotech-enabled human superintelligence at the same pace as frontier AI is the only way I can think of that respects the new minds we are building without handing over control to them.
